record.paper_title: Brane Supersymmetry Breaking and the Cosmological Constant: Open Problems
record.original_question: For concrete string compactifications containing stable non-BPS 3-branes, do the bulk supergravity fields actually acquire supersymmetry-breaking masses in the milli-electron-volt range predicted by volume suppression? Answering this requires solving for the eigenvalues of the scalar, fermion, gravitino, and related wave operators in the full gravitational background of the non-BPS soliton and determining whether the lowest bulk modes in realistic three-brane geometries, rather than only in toy models, scale as mbulk approximately mbrane squared divided by the Planck mass.

evidence.quote: It must be demonstrated in concrete examples that mbulk is really in the milli–eV range.
To actually compute the bulk masses precisely, one should find the eigenvalues of the various wave operators in the gravitational background of the non–BPS soliton

Generalizing the discussion to the three–brane geometry is left for the future; let us just note that it seems important to "get out of the throat", i.e. to not only restrict the discussion to the near–horizon limit AdS5 × S5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Type IIB-like string compactification to four dimensions with six compact transverse dimensions of large volume, containing a stable non-BPS 3-brane soliton extended along the four non-compact spacetime directions and breaking all bulk supersymmetries. The brane carries a localized supersymmetry-breaking scale m_brane (assumed to be of order TeV), and a heuristic volume-suppression argument suggests that supersymmetry breaking transmitted to the bulk supergravity sector should produce light bulk superpartners of the graviton (scalars, fermions, gravitini, etc.) with masses scaling as
   m_bulk ≈ m_brane² / M_Pl,
which for m_brane ~ TeV gives m_bulk in the milli-electron-volt range.

Problem. In a realistic (non-toy) string-theoretic three-brane background—i.e. solving the full ten-dimensional supergravity equations for the non-BPS soliton including the asymptotic region away from any near-horizon AdS₅ × S⁵ throat—determine the eigenvalues of the scalar, fermionic, gravitino, and related linearized wave operators governing fluctuations of the bulk supergravity fields. Show whether the lowest non-zero eigenvalues (the bulk-mode masses as seen by a four-dimensional observer after Kaluza–Klein reduction over the transverse compact space) indeed obey the scaling
   m_bulk ~ m_brane² / M_Pl
predicted by the volume-suppression heuristic, with m_bulk in the milli-eV range when m_brane ~ TeV. In particular, exhibit at least one concrete compactification with a stable non-BPS 3-brane in which this scaling can be derived rather than assumed.
artifact.category_tag: Brane supersymmetry breaking and bulk mass spectra
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal that the milli-eV bulk-mass prediction from m_bulk ~ m_brane²/M_Pl in non-BPS 3-brane compactifications is stated as a heuristic open issue: it has been discussed in subsequent brane-world supersymmetry-breaking literature, but no concrete realistic three-brane geometry computation (beyond the near-horizon AdS₅ × S⁵ toy models) demonstrating this scaling from the eigenvalues of the bulk wave operators appears to have been published. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Brane world supersymmetry breaking, Phys. Rev. D 65, 105011
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses transmission of brane SUSY breaking to bulk supergravity with volume-suppressed bulk masses, without providing concrete non-BPS 3-brane eigenvalue computations.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work develops the brane-world scenario but does not solve the bulk wave-operator spectrum in realistic non-BPS 3-brane backgrounds.

status_evidence.title: Asymmetric orientifolds, brane supersymmetry breaking and non-BPS branes
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs non-BPS branes with supersymmetry breaking in specific orientifold models.
status_evidence.claim: Stable non-BPS branes exist in concrete string constructions but explicit bulk-mode eigenvalue analyses confirming the milli-eV scaling have not been carried out.
